thread:
lena: Noticed a spike of SAST failures at 02:00 UTC, lots of identical decrypt errors from the scanner. Might be related to the RBAC change yesterday
lena: example: `ERROR: 403 PermissionDenied: serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com missing kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt on projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/sdlc/cryptoKeys/sast-key`
owen: we changed a role grant in the org-level group for `kb-team` last night to tighten access. Could be we removed the scanner-sa binding unintentionally
tesfa: pulling audit log now, filtering for `SetIamPolicy` on the sdlc key ring
tesfa: found an entry: `principals: terraform-sa applied policy remove members serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` at 01:47 UTC
vic: ugh, terraform drift. Which terraform run did that? stack shows `tf-apply/rotate-keystore`
ci-scanner: JOB_FAILED job=ci-sast-main-90123 reason=decrypt_error
ops-oncall: I can grant an emergency corridor binding for 30m, need an authorized request recorded in audit and a ticket link
lena: please do, granting request: ENGSEC-3827. Grant only `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/sdlc/cryptoKeys/sast-key`
ops-oncall: applying now: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding sast-key --keyring=sdlc --location=global --member=serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`
ops-oncall: audit log entry created: `iam.bind: ops-oncall -> serviceAccount:ci-scanner on sast-key (ttl=30m) ticket=ENGSEC-3827`
ci-scanner: JOB_REQUEUED job=ci-sast-main-90123
lena: after requeue, jobs are progressing. We should avoid mutating key-level policies via terraform in a way that removes known consumers.
tesfa: Agreed. Action items: 1) add terraform guardrail to prevent accidental removal of `scanner` SA, 2) add CI pre-check that validates `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` includes scanner-sa for active keys, 3) update rotation playbook to include 'notify consumers' step
own: I'll file a PR to `infra-keystore` to add a `prevent_destroy` lifecycle for the existing cryptoKey and attach bindings to an alias resource rather than raw key ids
vic: Also we had noisy duplicate findings because the aborted run left partial artifacts. We should ensure SAST triage ignores runs with `status: aborted` or `partial_archive`
ci-scanner: NOTE: partial_artifacts detected for run=2026-03-14T02:01:23Z mark=incomplete
lena: Good call. Marcus (cc'd in the playbook) had implemented evidence dedupe last quarter; can we extend it to skip aborted runs?
tesfa: I'll update the evidence service to reject findings from runs where `archive_complete=false`. Small patch and unit test.
ops-oncall: expired ephemeral grant (30m) - audit shows it was active for 18m. CI still passing after rerun. Closing emergency grant.
security-bot: INCIDENT: sast-decrypt-rbac (sev=medium) owner=eng-security actions=[ephemeral_grant,terraform_pr,precheck,playbook_update]
own: For postmortem: root cause = terraform rotation removed binding; contributing factors = missing pre-promotion validation, no prevent_destroy on key resource, evidence service surfacing partial runs. Recommended remediation tasks assigned in ENGSEC board
lena: Also adding a runbook tweak: when granting an ephemeral permission, include the exact `gcloud` command and require a linked ticket; that makes audits easier during IR
vic: propose adding an alert that looks for `SetIamPolicy` events that remove members from keys used by critical CI SAs. If triggered, auto-open a ticket to eng-security for verification
tesfa: wrote the audit query and alert rule draft, will open PR in `observability/alerts`
own: scheduling a dry-run rotation in staging this week to validate iam-sync and terraform lifecycle. Will include oncall and infra folks
lena: thanks all. I'll draft the postmortem and link to ENGSEC-3827. Closing thread once postmortem is posted
